legend: Dima and Inna are doing so great! At the moment, Inna is sitting on the magic lawn playing with a pink pony. Dima wanted to play too. He brought an n × m chessboard, a very tasty candy and two numbers a and b.

Dima put the chessboard in front of Inna and placed the candy in position (i, j) on the board. The boy said he would give the candy if it reaches one of the corner cells of the board. He's got one more condition. There can only be actions of the following types:
move the candy from position (x, y) on the board to position (x - a, y - b);
move the candy from position (x, y) on the board to position (x + a, y - b);
move the candy from position (x, y) on the board to position (x - a, y + b);
move the candy from position (x, y) on the board to position (x + a, y + b).
Naturally, Dima doesn't allow to move the candy beyond the chessboard borders.

Inna and the pony started shifting the candy around the board. They wonder what is the minimum number of allowed actions that they need to perform to move the candy from the initial position (i, j) to one of the chessboard corners. Help them cope with the task!
input: The first line of the input contains six integers n, m, i, j, a, b (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 106; 1 ≤ i ≤ n; 1 ≤ j ≤ m; 1 ≤ a, b ≤ 106).

You can assume that the chessboard rows are numbered from 1 to n from top to bottom and the columns are numbered from 1 to m from left to right. Position (i, j) in the statement is a chessboard cell on the intersection of the i-th row and the j-th column. You can consider that the corners are: (1, m), (n, 1), (n, m), (1, 1).
output: In a single line print a single integer — the minimum number of moves needed to get the candy.
If Inna and the pony cannot get the candy playing by Dima's rules, print on a single line "Poor Inna and pony!" without the quotes.
note: Inna and the pony can move the candy to position (1 + 2, 3 + 2) = (3, 5), from there they can move it to positions (3 - 2, 5 + 2) = (1, 7) and (3 + 2, 5 + 2) = (5, 7). These positions correspond to the corner squares of the chess board. Thus, the answer to the test sample equals two.

legend.ai: Dima 和 Inna 玩得非常开心！此时，Inna 正坐在魔法草坪上和一只粉色小马玩耍。Dima 也想一起玩。他带来了一块 n × m 的棋盘、一颗非常美味的糖果以及两个数 a 和 b。
Dima 把棋盘放在 Inna 面前，并将糖果放在棋盘上的位置 (i, j)。男孩说，如果糖果能够到达棋盘的某个角落格子，他就会把糖果给她。他还有一个条件：只能进行以下几种操作：
将棋盘上位于位置 (x, y) 的糖果移动到位置 (x - a, y - b)；
将棋盘上位于位置 (x, y) 的糖果移动到位置 (x + a, y - b)；
将棋盘上位于位置 (x, y) 的糖果移动到位置 (x - a, y + b)；
将棋盘上位于位置 (x, y) 的糖果移动到位置 (x + a, y + b)。
当然，Dima 不允许将糖果移出棋盘边界。
Inna 和小马开始在棋盘上移动糖果。他们想知道，将糖果从初始位置 (i, j) 移动到棋盘的某个角所需执行的允许操作的最少次数。请帮助他们完成这个任务！

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含六个整数 n、m、i、j、a、b（1 ≤ n, m ≤ 10^6；1 ≤ i ≤ n；1 ≤ j ≤ m；1 ≤ a, b ≤ 10^6）。
你可以认为棋盘的行从上到下编号为 1 到 n，列从左到右编号为 1 到 m。题目中的位置 (i, j) 表示第 i 行与第 j 列交叉处的棋盘格。你可以认为棋盘的四个角分别为：(1, m)、(n, 1)、(n, m) 和 (1, 1)。

output.ai: 请在一行中输出一个整数——获得糖果所需的最少移动次数。
如果 Inna 和小马无法按照 Dima 的规则获得糖果，请在一行中输出不带引号的 “Poor Inna and pony!”。

note.ai: Inna 和小马可以将糖果移动到位置 (1 + 2, 3 + 2) = (3, 5)，从那里可以将其移动到位置 (3 - 2, 5 + 2) = (1, 7) 和 (3 + 2, 5 + 2) = (5, 7)。这些位置对应于棋盘的角落格子。因此，测试样例的答案为 2。
